S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and disturbance in the way one’s body weight or shape is experienced or an undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation. Individuals often deny the seriousness of their low body weight and may exhibit rigid, perfectionistic thinking around food, exercise, and achievement. Onset is most common in adolescence and young adulthood, but it can occur or recur later in life, often in the context of stress, loss, or identity shifts. The course can be chronic and relapsing, and it is distinguished from other eating disorders by the marked underweight status and the primary focus on restriction rather than recurrent binge eating or compensatory behaviors alone.

patient.personality: Ansley is a gentle, methodical homemaker who finds comfort in orderly routines, nurturing others, and quiet, detail‑oriented creative work.
patient.stressor: Ansley’s problems started after she was told at a routine checkup that her blood pressure and cholesterol were creeping up, and she was advised to lose a bit of weight and exercise more to protect her heart. Already somewhat anxious about aging and determined not to become a “burden,” she threw herself into meal planning and portion control with the same meticulousness she applied to quilting patterns and genealogy charts. As friends at the senior center praised her for looking “so tiny” and she saw the numbers on the scale fall, controlling her food intake became a central way she felt in charge of her body and health, even as her portions grew smaller and mealtimes became increasingly rule‑bound. She agreed to see a psychiatrist only after her primary care physician, worried by her continued weight loss and frailty despite improved labs, urged an evaluation when she insisted she was simply being careful and could not understand why everyone was so worried about how little she was eating.
patient.chief_complaint: My doctor says I’ve lost too much weight and wants me to talk to someone about it, even though I feel like I’m just being careful with what I eat.

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: These days I measure out my meals like I’m following a sewing pattern, just a few spoonfuls of yogurt in the morning and a small salad or some steamed vegetables at night, and if I feel even the slightest bit full I tell myself I’ve overdone it and skip the next meal to make up for it.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: My clothes hang off me and I’ve had to punch extra holes in my belt, but I just think, well, the doctor wanted me to lose weight for my heart and I still see plenty of little places I could “trim down” if I really tried.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If I even think about adding a slice of bread or a bit of butter, I get this tight feeling in my chest and picture the number on the scale jumping up and my heart clogging up again, so I’d rather go to bed a little hungry than risk it.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.
S084.manifestation: Everyone keeps saying I look frail and that it’s dangerous at my age, but I honestly feel like they’re overreacting, because apart from getting tired sometimes I don’t feel sick, and it seems silly to make a fuss just because I finally have my weight under control.
